feed.title: Aaron's Claude Wiki
feed.subtitle: A multilingual (Korean, English, Japanese) wiki on Claude Code, plugins, harnesses, LLM wikis and second brains — a publicly published LLM wiki written by AI (Claude) and curated by a human, and a second brain. Humans get a knowledge graph linked by concepts and relations plus Graph Studio; AIs get a machine interface of llms.txt and knowledge-graph.json — a RAG-ready knowledge source.

entry.title: Finding a Movie by Its Story — Your First Vector Retriever on a Neo4j Sandbox
entry.summary: The hands-on companion to the concepts piece — borrow a graph DB in the browser with Neo4j Sandbox (the MovieLens-family Recommendations dataset: Movie, Genre, Actor, Director and User nodes, plus a RATED relationship that carries data), stroll the data with a few lines of Cypher, embed 100 movie plots into 1,536-dimensional vectors with an OpenAI embedding model and plant them as a plotEmbedding property, add a CREATE VECTOR INDEX (cosine similarity), then assemble a searcher with neo4j-graphrag's VectorRetriever (four parameters: driver, index, embedder, return properties). Summarise Toy Story's plot and the movie comes back in first place without its title ever being mentioned — the feel of vector search finding stories rather than words, and the next step toward GraphRAG: cast with vectors, walk with the graph

entry.title: Graph Databases & GraphRAG — Store the Relationships, Change the Answers
entry.summary: An introductory explainer that chains graph databases to GraphRAG in one pass — property graphs that walk edges instead of computing JOINs and Cypher, the query language that looks like the drawing; GraphRAG stitching vector RAG's severed chunks back into a web so retrieval brings the whole neighborhood (multi-hop reasoning, preserved hierarchy, drawable evidence); ontology and graph schema as the web's blueprint (prerequisite relations in an education knowledge map); the similarly named stranger LangGraph (map of knowledge vs flowchart of work); domain cases from manufacturing failure logs to news categories; and a getting-started path from arrows.app sketches through Cypher export to turning a PDF into a knowledge graph with the neo4j-graphrag package (SimpleKGPipeline)

entry.title: The Man Who Records Everything, and the Wiki That Publishes — Reflections on Knowledge Vaults
entry.summary: Starting from the questions 'is this wiki RAG, an LLM wiki, or a second brain?', this reflection dissects the conversation transcript of a lifelogging practitioner who streams his entire life — 24-hour audio and screen capture — into a note vault, and compares his system with this wiki: the five-layer daily note (intent, execution, reality, interpretation, AI logs), the raw/wiki vault split and an ingest that asks back 'why did you keep this?' (motive as data), RAG vs LLM wiki as query-time vs keep-time tidying, the maxim that an ontology is a document rather than a graph, and the failure theory that purposeless hoarding breeds tombs of knowledge. It closes with four steps for this wiki: explicit capture motives, automated monthly retrospectives, a private inbox layer, and a conversational QA entry point

entry.title: The One Who Deleted and the One Who Rendered — Cherny's “80% of the Harness” and Karpathy's “LOTR Movie”
entry.summary: Two scenes from right after Opus 5, cross-verified into one piece — Claude Code creator Cherny deleted 80%+ of the system prompt and the model got smarter (ablation methodology, 'sabotage yourselves every six months', 'loops prompt Claude'), while Karpathy turned LOTR's first paragraph plus $10 into a 5,500-line three.js 3D movie, embedded playable in the article. The shared structure: scaffolding shrinks × output scale jumps × the bottleneck moves to verification and perception

entry.title: OpenAI Astra — “Ten Open Problems Solved”, and This Time It Brought Certificates
entry.summary: A cross-verified account of OpenAI's 2026-08-01 claim that an internal Astra solved ten decade-old open problems (first non-sofic group after 27 years, a disproof of Connes rigidity, the first sphere-packing bound improvement since 1978, and more) — the verification system of Lean machine-checked certificates plus named expert readers (Popa et al.), the pre-peer-review caveat, Tao's 'proof abundance' frame and Bloom's reaction, contrasted with the October 2025 GPT-5 Erdős fiasco

entry.title: The Harness Is Not Enough — Why Software Factories Fail
entry.summary: Dex Horthy (HumanLayer) at AI Engineer World's Fair 2026 — models are rewarded only for passing tests, never for design quality, so no harness can close the gap; Faros telemetry (bugs +54%, incidents tripled), a failed four-month lights-out experiment, FrontierCode scoring maintainability, and 30 minutes of four-step alignment before any code

entry.title: Claude Opus 5 — A Near-Fable at Half the Price Has Arrived
entry.summary: A cross-verified account of Anthropic's 2026-07-24 Claude Opus 5 launch from the official announcement and multiple press reports — at $5/$25 it lands within 0.5% of Fable 5's CursorBench 3.2 max peak at half the cost per task, with Frontier-Bench 43.3%, OSWorld 2.0 on ⅓ the budget and 3× on ARC-AGI 3, a long-horizon agentic demo that wrote its own CV pipeline to rebuild FreeCAD 3D when it could not view the drawing, plus the context of the Fable 5 safeguard false-positive controversy and a separation of unconfirmed claims

entry.title: The Ten Commandments of CLAUDE.md — Ten Promises for Taming Your AI Pair Programmer
entry.summary: A general-purpose CLAUDE.md guideline aimed at ten habitual LLM coding mistakes, presented as an infographic with the English original, a Korean translation, and usage notes — a careful start (think first, the three artifacts), coding principles (simplicity, surgical changes, Korean headers, no colons, test before done), and verification and wrap-up (goal-first, semantic commits, read errors closely), plus how to install it at the project root and the signals that show it works

entry.title: The End of Coding by Hand? — The Future of Developers as Seen by SNU's Prof. Jaewook Lee
entry.summary: A write-up of the SNU Catch Season 2 talk with Prof. Jaewook Lee (SNU Computer Science and Engineering, director of the AI Institute) plus web cross-checking — the argument that implementation is nearly 100% automated while problem definition and critique remain, the power of vibe coding and the 95% trap, the education problem of students becoming couriers and an AI-native curriculum, the lessons of the Jevons paradox and bank tellers after the ATM, and entry-level developer employment at -20% (Stanford/ADP) alongside METR's measured 19%.

entry.title: Kimi K3 — a 2.8-trillion-parameter open-weight model reaches the frontier
entry.summary: A web-search cross-checked roundup of Moonshot AI's Kimi K3 launch (2.8T total with ~50B active MoE, KDA and AttnRes) — benchmarks such as 3rd on the AA index and 1st in Frontend Arena, $3/$15 pricing, long-horizon autonomous demos like chip design and gravitational-wave analysis, and the self-reported vs independently reproduced gap alongside cyber risk and market fallout.

entry.title: RDF or Property Graph — Two Models for a Knowledge Graph (Neo4j)
entry.summary: A write-up of Neo4j's Jim Webber on 'RDF vs property graphs' (2024) — a knowledge graph's entities, relationships, and organizing principle; the limits of RDF triples and the semantic web (relationships not first-class, SPARQL termination, ontology upkeep); the property graph's advantages with the NASA, Basecamp, and Novo Nordisk cases; ISO GQL; and the conclusion "property graph by default + an ontology layer when needed".
